summary: Sussex County, DE state tower erected 1931, staffed by towermen, used as an AWS unit in wartime, and removed between 2002 and 2006; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 with a seven-foot square cabin, upper half enclosed in glass
facts.status_note: Removed sometime between 2002 and 2006 after being turned over to State Police for communications purposes

staffing.status: Staffed by a towerman, per state forester reports of the 1930s and 1940s

facts.agency: Delaware state forestry department (annual reports of the State Forester)

events.note: Erection started July 29, 1931; towers opened for service October 15, 1931. FFLOS also gives 1931.
Towerman thinned the one-acre site on days his services were not needed in the cabin
Dark green curtains installed in the Dagsboro, Laurel and Ellendale towers to reduce glare
Cabin windows replaced with windows of a new design
Operated as an AWS unit during the war, per the FY1946 report. The war-time dates are not given; 1946 is the report year.
Wired for electric power following the radio installation contract; power supplied by Delaware Power and Light Company
Aluminum sliding windows purchased to replace the tower's windows
Turned over to State Police for communications purposes, then removed sometime between 2002 and 2006. The year is the earliest bound of that range, not a confirmed date.
Registered September 11, 2008 as FFLOS US 72, DE 3

corrections.why: Sources describe a 100-foot tower, 100 feet from the ground to the cabin floor and 110 feet overall. The 13.7 m value is about 45 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1931-32 state report places the site about 2 1/2 miles northeast of Laurel; the 1934 report says 3 miles. The story gives both figures and does not pick one.

The record's 11.6 m matches the association's 38 ft (12 m). The 1931 state report describes the site on a 45-foot elevation. The record keeps the association figure; the two may measure different things.

notes_for_editor: Removal date rests on the association's pages ('between 2002-2006'); no state or agency record was found, and the State Police hand-over has no date. 'AWS unit' is the state report's abbreviation and is not expanded in the source; the story keeps the term. Sources 3 and 4 are a fan site transcribing state annual reports, not the originals. No access, visit or current-condition data was found, so those keys are omitted. The record's height_m is corrected in corrections. One web search for Laurel and one for Ellendale-era Delaware history were used, shared with Ellendale.
